July 31, 2026

Cigna Appeals Department  
[Appeal mailing address from member ID card or Cigna instructions]

Re: Expedited/Pre-Service Medical Necessity Appeal  
Member: Taylor Jennings  
Member ID: W530749089  
Plan: Cigna Commercial/ACA, Illinois  
Reference number: POC-F7C299C469-49918  
Requested service: Lumbar decompression/microdiscectomy  
CPT: 63030  
Surgeon: Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery  

Dear Cigna Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing Cigna’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, lumbar disc surgery/decompression. The denial states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria. Based on the clinical evidence submitted with the prior authorization request, the procedure is medically necessary for Taylor Jennings’ persistent, function-limiting lumbar radiculopathy caused by an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe nerve-root compression.

I respectfully request that Cigna overturn the denial and authorize the requested surgery.

Clinical basis for medical necessity

1. Persistent and progressive symptoms

Taylor has experienced 14 months of progressive lower-back pain that has not resolved with rest. The symptoms include radicular pain extending into the right calf. Taylor cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, demonstrating substantial impairment in ordinary daily functioning.

2. Failure of appropriate conservative treatment

Taylor completed a structured course of supervised physical therapy focused on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility. The treatment lasted 12 weeks, from April 10, 2026, through July 3, 2026, and included 16 completed visits. The physical therapy discharge note documents this treatment.

Taylor also used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief. A corticosteroid injection administered on April 20, 2026, produced only two weeks of partial relief. The persistence of symptoms despite medication, injection therapy, and a full supervised rehabilitation course supports escalation to surgical treatment.

3. Objective imaging showing a surgically relevant lesion

Lumbar MRI performed on June 8, 2026, demonstrated an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This is an objective structural abnormality that corresponds to Taylor’s right-sided radicular symptoms and functional limitations.

4. Concordant examination findings

The clinical examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. The examination findings, MRI findings, and right-calf radicular symptoms are anatomically and clinically concordant.

5. Absence of documented contraindications

The submitted records document no active infection and no untreated substance-use disorder. Taylor is a nonsmoker and has a BMI of 29. These facts do not provide a medical reason to withhold the requested decompression procedure.

Why CPT 63030 is appropriate

The requested operation is directed at decompressing the affected lumbar nerve root at the level of the L4-L5 disc extrusion. Taylor has persistent symptoms, failed substantial conservative treatment, objective severe lateral recess stenosis with L5 nerve-root compression, functional impairment, and corresponding neurologic findings. Together, these records support the medical necessity of surgical decompression rather than continued ineffective conservative care.

The records provided to me do not include the exact plan language or the specific clinical-review criteria applied to this request. I have therefore not quoted the plan’s policy. Please provide, as part of this appeal, the exact policy and criteria version used for reference number POC-F7C299C469-49918, the clinical rationale for the denial, and any specific documentation Cigna believes is missing.

Please have an appropriately qualified physician review the complete record, including:

- The June 8, 2026 lumbar MRI report and images, if required;
- The physical therapy discharge note documenting 16 visits from April 10 through July 3, 2026;
- The medication history documenting six months of inadequate response to NSAIDs;
- The April 20, 2026 corticosteroid injection record and limited two-week partial response;
- The orthopedic examination documenting positive provocative testing and the corresponding neurologic deficit; and
- The surgical recommendation from Okafor, MD.

Because Taylor has severe functional limitation and ongoing nerve-root-related symptoms, I request a prompt pre-service appeal determination. Please send the written appeal decision, the clinical rationale, and instructions for any further appeal or external review to the address on file.

Sincerely,

Taylor Jennings
